task: Audit this provisional English against the supplied Ge’ez transcriptions of five consecutive manuscript sides. Identify at most 12 material issues: missing recoverable meaning, unsupported assertions, negation/speaker reversals, names/numbers, silent harmonisation, or broken joins. Distinguish true English problems from source ambiguity. Do not replace the text with familiar scripture; do not claim image verification, expert approval or numerical accuracy. The source is machine transcribed and may be wrong. Give exact side, block index and line references. Evaluate full coverage, including apparently fluent text and boundaries, not only brackets. Return a concise JSON object.

blocks.english: ...our word [ቀለነ, likely ቃልነ]. And concerning this we ask for them of him who sent me, that we may [understand / ንለብክ unclear] and teach them the tidings of the holy gospel.
uncertainties: ቀለነ: taken as ቃልነ 'our word'; vowel uncertain
ንለብክ: unfamiliar form; perhaps ንለቡ 'we understand'; tentative
ዜና ወንጊል: ወንጊል taken as ወንጌል 'gospel'

blocks.english: And my Lord said to us: 'He who heard you [i.e. hears you], he who received you, has received [ተወክሮ, read ተወክፈ?] him who sent me, [እሉየ: these/me?]; for [እሉየ: these/I?] and I, we are one. And those who hear you hear me [ዓኀበራ: unclear] for the holy church.'
uncertainties: ተወክሮ: unexpected form; context suggests ተወክፈ 'received'
እሉየ (twice): unresolved; could be 'these (are) mine' or a corruption of ኪያየ 'me'
ዓኀበራ (line 10): unresolved; possibly 'together with/for' (ኅብረ?) — left as gap
ወለ ስምዑ: read as ወእለ ሰምዑ 'and those who hear'

blocks.english: We stand for them in the heavens, as concerning this our word which they heard.
And they kept [it] and made [ጥቁሙ: it exact/firm?] while not abandoning the canon of the holy church; we stand for them in the heavens.
uncertainties: ጥቁሙ: unclear; perhaps ጥዩቀ 'exactly' or ጥቀ 'very'; tentative

blocks.english: For we are stewards [gatherers] of the ordinance of God; they will become children of God. We ordained by our word that we ourselves might entrust them with our God.
uncertainties: ሠራዓነ: taken as 1pl 'we ordained'; could be 'our ordinance'

blocks.english: God said to Moses: 'I entrust them [to ...] [ለያቁቆ: to Jacob? unclear] Levi[te(s)?]...'
uncertainties: ለያቁቆ: unresolved; perhaps ለያዕቆብ 'to Jacob' or a damaged form
ሌዊ: 'Levi' or beginning of 'Levites'; side ends mid-clause

boundary_notes: Side begins mid-sentence (ቀለነ ends a prior clause).
Side ends mid-clause at ሌዊ; 169V line 1 does not obviously continue the sentence—see cross-side issues.

blocks.english: ...the [vessels: ንቀየ, perhaps ንዋየ] of the [ትእቢት: unclear] tabernacle, that they may keep [them] and [ደግለሠኢ: unresolved] and make and do the work of the tabernacle, and honour all the [vessels] of the work of the holy tabernacle, [እ?ዝት: unclear]; they shall not [remove: ኢያስስሉ] and shall not turn aside from what is commanded in the law which God ordained for the tabernacle of righteousness which is in the heavens.
uncertainties: Throughout this side ደ appears where ይ expected (ደቀቡ=ይዕቀቡ, ደግበራ=ይግበሩ, ደጸውም=ይጸውም, ደቤ=ይቤ)

blocks.english: And moreover [ወበደግምስ = ወበዳግምስ] he showed Moses the work of the tabernacle while not diminishing from what he showed Moses on Mount Sinai where he spoke with him in a pillar of cloud, so that he fasted forty days and forty nights that he might speak with God. And Moses himself said:

Speaker: continuation of Moses' first-person speech from 169V

blocks.english: And again, that I may offer to him a sacrifice of righteousness to God, which is freewill and salvation; and with sacrifice which is for sin, and the perpetual sacrifice of salvation, and the sacrifice of praise, and the sacrifice which is according to its law for the year, in the holy church.

blocks.english: This my Lord commanded me, that I should [make good / ordain: እሠኒ] the work of the holy tabernacle, its pattern [እርእያሃ = አርአያሃ] of the holy one, of that which is to be made in the last days, which is the bride, the soul of Christians, which he redeemed by the blood of the Messiah.

blocks.english: And again Moses said: 'I saw a [ጣጠስ: unclear—bush?] of fire burning, and I approached that I might ascertain its [terror/awe: ግርማሁ], and a voice came out from within...

blocks.english: ...-in that fire, and said to me: "Take off your sandal(s) [እሠዕኒክ = አሣእኒከ] from your feet, for the land where you stand is holy; it is the church."

And that [ውእቱኪ = ውእቱኒ?] also, the whole of it, its appearance [መርእዊሃ] the lampstand which was spoken of; and its pillars of gold [ጸዕልት: unclear—pure?], which they say are the apostles, [if/they are: እመንቱ] those whose right hand(s) [were] like a strong pillar in all that [ዘእሠመርዎሙ: pleased them? / was appointed for them?], before kings and rulers and in all the hands of the Jews [እደሁ|ይ]...

blocks.english: ...[Jews] and apostate peoples, who [made them stand / did not stand them: ኢቀውምዎሙ] in the court, that they might beat them and judge them and bring down their right hands from what was raised; it did not yield [ኢይየውሕ], and they did not say "yes" [እሁ] at the command of their own [masters?], and they did not bring down their right hands from what was raised—

uncertainties: ኢሰዝብጠቱ: read ኢበዝብጠት 'not by beating'; form corrupt

uncertainties: ኢያውርድ: singular 'he/one did not bring down' with plural hands; subject ambiguous

blocks.english: And likewise, after its pattern [እርእያሁ], the martyrs do, until they gave up their souls; [the world abandoned them / they abandoned the world: ኀደጎሙ ዓለሙ] and all that is in it, the light of the world, the sun and gold...
uncertainties: ኀደጎሙ ዓለሙ: subject/object ambiguous; both readings given

cross_side_issues: 169R→169V: 169R ends mid-clause (ለያቁቆ ሌዊ) and 169V begins ንቀየ ትእቢት ደብተራ; no clear syntactic continuation—possible lost text or the clause continues loosely ('...Levi[tes] [to keep] the vessels of the tabernacle'). Join left unresolved.

Orthography: 169V and 170V frequently write ደ for ይ (prefix of imperfect/ይቤ); 169R/170R use ይ. Also እ for አ/ዐ throughout (እግዚእብሔር, እነ, እምላክ, እርእያ). These are read as spelling variants, not emended silently.

Speaker tracking: 169R first-person plural ('we') likely apostolic/ecclesial voice, then God to Moses; 169V–170R Moses first-person; 170V–171R third-person exposition on Ezra, Zechariah, apostles, martyrs.
